summary: This Letter generalizes analytical fidelity-reduction formulae from static to time-dependent Markovian dissipation, enabling prediction of average gate fidelity for quantum operations where decoherence rates vary during execution. Application to adiabatic controlled-Z gates in superconducting circuits reveals that flux-dependent noise sensitivity and qubit-coupler hybridization significantly degrade fidelity in tunable architectures.
motivation: Baseband flux gates in superconducting quantum computers dynamically modulate qubit or coupler frequencies, causing dissipation rates to become time-dependent, but existing analytical fidelity formulae assume static noise and thus fail for these increasingly common tunable architectures.
method: The authors extend the Lindblad master equation framework with time-dependent dissipative rates $\Gamma_k(t)$ and expand the average gate fidelity $\bar{F}$ to first order in the small parameter $\bar{\Gamma}_k \tau$, showing that each dissipative process contributes independently via time-dependent jump operators $\hat{L}(t)$ evolved in the Heisenberg picture.
result: The generalized fidelity formula $\bar{F} = 1 + \sum_k \int_0^\tau dt\, \Gamma_k(t)\, \delta F[\hat{L}_k(t)]$ provides a rigorous bound for adiabatic operations, revealing that interplay between parameter-dependent noise channels and mode hybridization fundamentally restricts achievable fidelity in flux-tuned superconducting quantum computers.
